channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Wider Europe Briefing: Ukraine's 2027 EU Dream And What Brussels Wants From Moscow
item.description: Could Ukraine really join the EU next year?

item.title: EU Quizzes Ukraine On Timeline For Repair Of Druzhba Oil Pipeline
item.description: A European Commission spokeswoman on February 17 confirmed that Brussels was in touch with Ukraine regarding the Druzhba pipeline that has been damaged since late January, preventing Russian oil from flowing to Hungary and Slovakia.

item.title: Teen Kickbox Champ Killed in War Honored On Banned Olympic Helmet
item.description: Karina Bakhur, a 17-year-old kickboxing champion killed by a Russian missile in Ukraine, is honored on Ukrainian Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych’s helmet. He was banned from competing in skeleton for the tribute. Bakhur's father says he is proud that his daughter's memory lives on.

item.title: State Department: No 'Gentleman's Agreement' Between US, Russia On Expired Nuclear Treaty
item.description: A senior US State Department official has flatly rejected suggestions that Washington and Moscow are informally continuing to observe the limits of the now-expired, nuclear-weapon-limiting New START treaty, saying there is no “gentlemen’s agreement” in place.

item.title: Archaeologists Launch 'Virtual Museum' To Ukraine's Ancient Heritage
item.description: An online museum aims to make Ukraine’s heritage accessible to the public while many of the featured treasures remain impossible to view in person.

item.title: Zelenskyy Says 'Progress' In Military Talks In Geneva, Political Talks 'Not Easy'
item.description: A second day of talks between Russia and Ukraine have broken up after around two hours in Geneva, Switzerland, with officials from both countries saying negotiations were "difficult."

item.title: Iran's 40-Day Mourning Ceremonies Spark Renewed Protests
item.description: Across Iran, memorials to mark 40 days since thousands of protesters were killed in January have turned into anti-government demonstrations.

item.title: Iranians Show Defiance Amid Memorials For Dead Protesters
item.description: With chants of "Death to Khamenei," directed at Iran's supreme leader, mourners in Iran were defiant as they gathered to mark 40 days since the deadly January 8-9 crackdown by security forces that killed thousands of protesters.

item.title: 'Made in Kosovo': New Barcode Could Boost Exports After Years Of Borrowed Labels
item.description: Kosovo has secured its own international barcode prefix, allowing products to be identified globally as “Made in Kosovo” for the first time. Producers say the move strengthens export visibility, though broader economic challenges remain.

item.title: Azadi Tower: Architect Watches From Exile As Beloved Iranian Landmark Coopted By Regime
item.description: Soon after his most famous public monument was completed, Hossein Amanat was forced to flee Iran amid the Islamic revolution. The architect spoke to RFE/RL about watching his Azadi Tower being used as a backdrop for Islamic regime military parades.
